title: ReviewPackage — the frozen review subject (root) + ReviewResult ($defs/reviewResult)
description: Bounded, non-recursive semantic review (V3-D6, contract §8). The package is the frozen floor of the review — the guaranteed minimum evidence set the executor must deliver, never a ceiling on what the reviewer may read at the pinned revisions: exact revision + locator + digest per member, never a byte copy of every source (invariant 9). Membership is by reference precisely so a package cannot become a second copy of the work that then drifts from it. An executor summary may be attached but is supplemental only — a package carrying a summary and no actual subjects is not a review subject at all (N2-A1). ReviewResult is owned solely by the independent reviewer (V3-D5); the controller may bind it but may never restate it with stronger meaning. REVIEWED_NO_BLOCKER means only 'no blocking discrepancy found within the frozen subjects and review dimensions' — it is never a proof of correctness, and no field anywhere below records one (N2-A3).

repair_round.description: 0 = the original candidate C reviewed by FULL; 1 = C2, the single user-approved repair, reviewed by VERIFY (V3-D6).

candidate_ref.description: The exact payload candidate under review. The commit is required here even though candidateRef leaves it optional: a review bound to a branch name alone would follow the branch as it moves, which is the 'review candidate A, accept candidate B' failure the digests elsewhere exist to prevent.

frozen_by.description: The controller that froze the subjects. Freezing is a binding act, not a judgment: it fixes WHAT is reviewed and never contributes an opinion about it (V3-D5).

executor_summary_ref.description: Optional executor-written summary. SUPPLEMENTAL ONLY (invariant 9): it never substitutes for a member, and the required-role assertions below hold regardless of whether it is present.

allOf.description: The raw frozen instruction must be in the package: FULL rechecks instruction-to-obligation completeness against it, and a reviewer given only the derived unit map cannot see an omission the map itself made (V3-D7, invariant 10).
At least one ACTUAL candidate artifact. This is the assertion that makes summary-only substitution fail (N2-A1).

reviewRound.description: One FULL, then at most one targeted VERIFY after a user-approved repair. No third round and no review-of-review exists (V3-D6, N2-A11).

memberRole.description: Closed logical membership of a ReviewPackage (invariant 9). 'source_input' is conditional because a WorkSpec may declare no inputs; 'check_result' is conditional because every obligation may be review_only. Both are still required to be COMPLETE when they exist, which the reviewer module enforces against the run rather than the schema — the schema cannot see how many results a run produced.

ref.description: Exact bytes by path + digest. There is deliberately no field here that could hold content: membership binds subjects, it never copies them (invariant 9).

locator.description: Optional in-file location when the member is a section rather than a whole file.

then.description: Members that come out of a tree must pin their revision as well as their digest. A digest alone says 'these bytes'; the revision says WHICH TREE those bytes were taken from, which is the disclosure N0-record R1 exists for. Generated control documents (plan, fulfillment, manifest, coverage, check results) live in the control root rather than in a reviewed tree, so a digest binds them completely.

result.description: The reviewer's own recheck of instruction-unit coverage against the raw instruction (invariant 10). It is deliberately NOT the InstructionCoverageAudit's enum: the audit is a pre-start preflight over a proposed map, this is a post-candidate recheck, and giving them one shared enum would invite a later reader to treat one as re-running the other.

instruction_ref.description: The exact raw instruction rechecked — the same frozen bytes the WorkSpec names, not the derived unit map.

unmapped_unit_ids.description: Instruction units the reviewer found normative but unmapped. Present only when there are some; never an empty placeholder.

then.description: An incompleteness claim that says nothing about what is missing cannot be acted on, and cannot be checked either. `unmapped_unit_ids` became required alongside `detail` at the V3 revise round: prose alone cannot be joined to anything, while an enumerated id set is what the finding and the residual are checked against downstream, and it is what a later WorkSpec revision maps. The ids are the reviewer's own — a unit the map omitted has no id in the WorkSpec to borrow, which is the whole point.

instructionCompleteness.description: V3 never claims an AI proved every semantic implication was enumerated (V3-D7). This records that the recheck happened and what it found.

disposition.description: SUPPORTED = the reviewer established the claim from evidence at the pinned revisions — package members or beyond them; when the establishing evidence goes beyond the package, that coverage is disclosed in `note` or `residual_uncertainty` (deliberately no dedicated field: the package is a floor on evidence, never a ceiling). NOT_SUPPORTED = the evidence CONTRADICTS the claim. UNVERIFIABLE = the reviewer could not establish it either way — including when the evidence that would settle it is not reachable at the pinned revisions, a state the earlier wording left ambiguous between the last two. UNVERIFIABLE is a REPORTED state and never silently folded into SUPPORTED — making the unverified visible is the endpoint this product actually promises (V3-D3, V3-D5, contract §1).

then.description: A negative or unestablished disposition must say why. An unexplained NOT_SUPPORTED cannot produce a minimum repair boundary, and an unexplained UNVERIFIABLE cannot be judged by the user who has to decide whether to accept it.

obligation_id.description: Present when the finding is about one obligation; absent when it is about the instruction map or the candidate as a whole.

blocking.description: Whether this finding blocks acceptance. A non-blocking finding is stated plainly as a finding rather than inflated into a blocker: an inflated blocker burns the single permitted repair round on something that was never a gate condition.

candidate_locator.description: Where in the candidate the problem is.

ground_truth_locator.description: Where in the instruction, source or plan the requirement it violates is.

minimum_fix.description: The smallest change that would resolve this finding. This is the text a REPAIR decision's boundary is derived from, which is why a blocking finding cannot omit it.

then.description: A blocker names where it is, what it violates and the smallest fix — or it is not a blocker. Without all three the user cannot bound a repair, and an unbounded repair is how the single permitted round turns into an open rewrite.

accepted_finding_ids.description: The findings the user accepted for repair — exactly the set the VERIFY is answerable for.

repair_diff_reviewed.description: Whether the ENTIRE repair diff was reviewed, not only the lines the accepted findings named. False is a legal, recorded state: an unreviewed remainder is where an unrelated change rides along, and a VERIFY that quietly skipped it must say so rather than report the same shape as one that did not.

permanent_boundaries_checked.description: Whether the boundaries that hold regardless of round were re-checked (V3-D6: VERIFY covers findings, the whole repair diff AND permanent boundaries).

verifyScope.description: Required on a VERIFY result, absent on a FULL. It makes the round's scope a stated fact rather than an assumption a later reader has to make.

package_ref.description: The exact frozen ReviewPackage this verdict answers for. A verdict that does not bind its package could be re-attributed to a different subject. The digest is `canonical_digest(package)` — computed over the package's canonical JSON (NFC-normalized, sorted keys, compact separators), NOT over the package file's bytes: `sha256sum review-package.json` will not reproduce it, and a CRLF checkout must not change package identity. The value reaches the reviewer out-of-band from the dispatching party; reproduce it from ResearchSystem/tooling with: python -c "from rsclib.document_harness import load_json; from rsclib.document_harness.review import package_digest; print(package_digest(load_json('<review-package.json>')))"

candidate_ref.description: The exact candidate reviewed, carried independently of the package so a mismatch between the two is detectable rather than assumed away.

verdict.description: Closed control verdicts (contract §5). Narrowed per round below. REVIEWED_NO_BLOCKER means only 'no blocking discrepancy found within the frozen subjects and review dimensions'.

per_obligation_disposition.description: Every obligation exactly once (invariant 2, N2-A2). The schema can require non-emptiness and reject duplicate whole rows; that the set matches the WorkSpec's obligations exactly is enforced by the reviewer module, which is the only place both documents are present.

findings.description: Present only when there are findings; absent means none were raised, following the same 'absence is not an empty placeholder' rule as the rest of v3.

residual_uncertainty.description: Disclosed uncertainty as DATA — never a fourth control verdict (V3-D6). This field deliberately breaks the 'absent means none' convention used elsewhere and is REQUIRED, empty array permitted: an omitted field cannot be distinguished from 'the reviewer never considered it', while an empty array is a positive statement that none was found. The user may convert these into ACCEPT_WITH_LIMITATIONS limitations.

reviewed_by.description: The independent reviewer that owns this result. Never the executor of the same run (V3-D5). Comparing declared names is all this can establish — role separation is a workflow protocol, not an OS guarantee (contract §1).

then.description: A VERIFY cannot return CHANGES_REQUIRED (contract §5): there is no second repair for it to request. A remaining blocker stops the run instead.
A FULL has no accepted-finding scope to declare — it is the round that produces the findings.
CHANGES_REQUIRED with no findings would demand a change without naming one.

reviewResult.description: One bounded review result (sole owner: the independent reviewer).
